# 2 Baruch Chapter 54 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** The Cloud and Waters Vision

---

**1** And thereupon I awoke, and I arose, and I prayed and said:

**2** "O Lord, you show me much and teach me many things, but you show me now something whose meaning I am not able to understand.

**3** The vision has comforted me in part, but in part it has troubled me; for I have seen things I cannot explain.

**4** "I entreat you therefore, O Lord my God, to interpret this vision for me.

**5** For I know that those things which I asked for earlier you have shown me;

**6** and now, I pray you to show me also the interpretation of this vision.

**7** "For at the end of the world retribution will come for the wicked, and for the righteous a new world will be opened.

**8** And because we have not received that world, we have not been found worthy of it;

**9** but because we have suffered much in this world, therefore we have been found worthy of the world to come.

**10** "For of all the things which the world has that is coming — man cannot know.

**11** For not for man has this world been created, but for man has the world to come been prepared.

**12** For this world is to man a trouble and a weariness with much labour; and that world to come will be a crown with great glory.

**13** "O Lord, I therefore cry out to you, and I ask of you: do not let my sin and my transgression prevail against me;

**14** and remember me before you, and let not the deeds of men prevail against me.

**15** For since the beginning I have been your servant, and I have given myself over to your service.

**16** "Now therefore I entreat you, O Lord God: let your mercy be great upon us, and let it not come upon us according to our deeds,

**17** but according to your loving-kindness.

**18** "For if you reward us according to our works, we have nothing with which to answer you.

**19** For what are we that we should speak to you? For we are dust before you.

**20** O Lord our God, save us for your name's sake.

**21** "For you have created us, and you have mercy upon those you have created; and you do not forsake your creatures.

**22** For every man who has been born has sinned; but you, O Lord, forgive them and have mercy on them."

---

*LOGOS notes: Formal equivalence rendering from the Syriac (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1). Paragraph divisions follow the sense units of the source.*
